html:
Bavaria was a large Catholic state in southern Germany, ruled from Munich by the Wittelsbach family for more than seven hundred years. On the map from 1783 to 1815 it is an electorate of the Holy Roman Empire, and from 1806 a kingdom.

Bavaria feared being swallowed by its neighbour, the Austrian Habsburgs, so it allied with Napoleon. He rewarded it with land, including Franconian cities such as Nuremberg, and made its elector a king in 1806. It joined the Confederation of the Rhine, then switched sides in 1813 in time to keep most of its gains.

In 1818 it got one of the first constitutions in Germany. Bavaria fought on Austria's side against Prussia in 1866 and lost, and in 1871 it joined the German Empire, keeping its own king and army in peacetime. Ludwig II built his fairy tale castles in these years. The monarchy fell in the revolution of 1918.
